en: The dyad of "dissociated from the taints and with taints," and the dyad of "root."

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints (*āsava*), is subject to the taints (*sāsava*), and is a root-cause (*hetu*), there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints, is not subject to the taints (*anāsava*), and is not a root-cause, by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*) … one.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints, is not subject to the taints, and is a root-cause, there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints, is not subject to the taints, and is not a root-cause, by way of root-condition … three.
(Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are four; under object-condition (*ārammaṇa*) there are two … pe … under non-disappearance-condition (*avigata*) there are four.

Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints (*āsava*), is subject to the taints (*sāsava*), and is not a root (*na-hetu*), there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints, is not subject to the taints, and is not a root, by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*). Dependent on a state that is dissociated from the taints, is not subject to the taints, and is not a root, there arises a state that is dissociated from the taints, is not subject to the taints, and is not a root, by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. There are two [answers] for root; ... pe ... two for non-disappearance (*avigata*).
